text:
anna: thinking out loud — we need a proposal for tenant-scoped ephemeral debug windows that automatically escalate redaction when a tenant's log/quota burn spikes. current inspect window is too blunt and exposes PII during bursts.
mike: +1. can you sketch the flow? is this a sampling change, a redact policy, or both?
anna: both. idea: each tenant gets a short debug window (e.g. 10m) when they opt-in. we track two signals: quota_burn_rate and sampled_inspect_rate. if quota_burn_rate > threshold we progressively tighten PII redaction and drop inspect payloads. keep a graceful degrade path.
ria: what do you mean by "progressively tighten"? levels?
anna: yeah — propose three levels: minimal (full inspect), masked (names/emails hashed + attachments removed), and scrubbed (no request/response bodies, only metadata and traces). transition rules by simple tokenized score.
oleg: ok but we need deterministic transitions so console can show state. suggest thresholds expressed as percent of committed capacity: e.g., if burn > 50% => masked, > 90% => scrubbed.
mike: agree. also need a soft-failover to a cheaper model variant rather than just scrub for latency-sensitive flows.
anna: good call. add routing policy: when scrubbed, route to route.debug_proxy that strips bodies and returns minimal provenance. config example:

```
inspect_window:
  duration_seconds: 600
  enabled: true
  escalation:
    - name: masked
      when: quota_burn_pct >= 50
      actions: [hash_pii, strip_attachments]
    - name: scrubbed
      when: quota_burn_pct >= 90
      actions: [drop_bodies, keep_headers]
```

ria: console UX: show tenant badge with current escalation level + reason (quota_burn_pct/last_5m). users should be able to request a one-time manual override with audit ticket.
oleg: ops-bot should emit events to the audit log when transitions happen. event names: `inspect.escalation.changed` and include {tenant_id, prev, next, reason}. keep payload minimal.
ops-bot: note — automated event hooks can be emitted to the existing audit stream. configure `emit_escalation_events: true` at tenant-level.
mike: telemetry: add metrics `tenant.inspect.escalation_level{tenant}` and `tenant.quota.burn_pct{tenant}`. dashboards need a compact per-tenant indicator for oncall.
anna: edgecases: what about routes that must never scrub (legal/compliance)? add per-route allowlist `inspect_never_scrub: true`. that should override escalation but still count against quota.
ria: and for visibility, console should surface the last raw-sampled payload timestamp (if present) and a link to request replay (subject to audit).
oleg: implementation notes — runtime should evaluate escalation every 30s, using moving avg over 5m. keep decisions idempotent and stored in control-plane so debounces survive restarts.
mike: sounds solid. next step: anna + oleg make a short RFC, include config schema, sample dashboard mock, and a roll-out plan with canary tenants.
anna: will draft today. assign reviewers: @mike @ria. thanks — will post RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
